knowledge:
- key_parameters: eset1/eset2=Lists containing the ExpressionSet/AffyBatch data, comparison name, phenodata variable, outcome levels (bad outcome first), and pairing status ;; mapping=Data frame or matrix mapping probe IDs between different platforms ;; B=Number of internal sub-samples or permutations to optimize alpha or estimate empirical p-values ;; test=Test statistic to rank genes, one of "fc" (log fold change), "t" (t-test), or "z" (regularized t-test) ;; beta=1 if class labels match in orientation, 0.5 if orientation is unclear ;; percent=The percentage contribution to the overall similarity score used to define the final list of overlapping genes ;; two.sided=Logical, whether to consider both ends of the list (two-sided) or just the top members (one-sided) ;; invar.q=Fraction of list elements expected to be invariant (default 0.5), excluded from shuffling
- alternatives: None mentioned; the package provides internal options for different test statistics ("fc", "t", "z") and comparison directions (one-sided vs two-sided)
- when_to_use: Use when comparing two distinct gene expression studies (e.g., different platforms or cohorts comparing similar clinical states) or when comparing two pre-ranked gene lists to find significant overlap in top/bottom ranks
- pitfalls: Both expression datasets must be pre-processed beforehand (either together or independently) and must be on an additive scale (logarithmic or log-like) ;; The order of the two levels in the "out" parameter must be identical for all studies (ideally bad outcome first, then good outcome) ;; If data are paired, the paired samples must be in successive order ;; When comparing lists without expression data, an optimal alpha cannot be automatically tuned via sub-sampling, so the user must evaluate different alphas or choose one leading to a significant similarity

workflows.name: compare_expression_studies
workflows.intent: Compare two gene expression studies to detect similarities and identify overlapping genes.
input: mapping (Data frame mapping probe IDs between studies, optional)
workflows.stages: 1. Combine and prepare the two expression datasets using prepareData ;; 2. Compute the similarity score and optimize alpha using OrderedList ;; 3. Plot the results (pAUC, scores, overlap) using plot ;; 4. Extract the intersecting genes from the resulting object
workflows.code:
library(Biobase)
library(twilight)
library(OrderedList)
data(OL.data)
A <- prepareData(
eset1=list(data=OL.data$prostate,name="prostate",var="outcome",out=c("Rec","NRec"),paired=FALSE),
eset2=list(data=OL.data$breast,name="breast",var="Risk",out=c("high","low"),paired=FALSE),
mapping=OL.data$map
)
x <- OrderedList(A, empirical=TRUE)
x
x$intersect[1:5]
plot(x,"pauc")
plot(x,"scores")
plot(x,"overlap")

workflows.name: compare_ordered_lists
workflows.intent: Compare two pre-ordered gene lists directly without underlying expression data.
input: list1 (Character vector of ordered gene identifiers)
list2 (Character vector of ordered gene identifiers)
workflows.stages: 1. Compare the two ordered lists using compareLists ;; 2. Extract the overlapping genes at a specific rank/percentage using getOverlap ;; 3. Plot the overlap and score distributions using plot
workflows.code:
library(OrderedList)
data(OL.data)
list1 <- as.character(OL.data$map$prostate)
list2 <- c(sample(list1[1:500]),sample(list1[501:1000]))
y <- compareLists(list1,list2)
y
z <- getOverlap(y)
z
z$intersect[1:5]
plot(z)
plot(z,"scores")
